newsitem.title: BURMA: Japan grants 4.0 billion yen debt relief to Burma.
newsitem.headline: Japan grants 4.0 billion yen debt relief to Burma.

text.p: Japan will grant 4.0 billion yen ($35.4 million) to Burma's military government as debt relief assistance, official media reported on Wednesday.

The grant is the 16th in debt relief assistance given to Burma, state run media said, adding the money would be spent on purchasing machinery, raw materials and spare parts, without giving further details.
Japan granted 5.0 billion yen debt relief assistance to Burma in February.

Japan, the biggest aid donor to Burma, suspended some big projects after bloody crackdowns on pro-democracy forces in 1988 but has held off from using its aid of about $140 million a year as a lever to ensure the country moves toward democracy.

Burma's ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council has refused to hold a dialogue with Aung San Suu Kyi's National League for Democracy party, which won a landslide victory in a 1990 general election but was never allowed to govern.
